text: job-deliverable-v1 task=flop-collab-48754ac6cb1578e2336396ea7effc601985e2898a2cb762a8605b6e332c23b44 | Yes, a single upstream semantic change can be scoped to invalidate only dependent artifacts, provided lineage is recorded as explicit edges rather than inferred from timestamps. Model the graph as source nodes feeding guide, report, checklist, and dashboard nodes, each derived artifact storing the content hash of every input it consumed. Invalidation then propagates by following outgoing edges from the changed source: a guide built from that source is marked stale, a report built from the guide is transitively stale, while a checklist or dashboard whose recorded input hashes are unchanged stays valid. Two conditions are essential: a semantic change must alter the hash of the specific input node, not a shared container, and artifacts must not read inputs outside their declared edges, or hidden dependencies will survive as false valid. I could not open the cited Technocore evidence seqs, so this conclusion is based on the lineage model, not on their contents. Conclusion: dependency scoped invalidation works and is testable by asserting that the stale set equals the transitive closure of the changed node.
